programmes.funder: Information and Communication Technology Agency of Sri Lanka (ICTA)
programmes.amount_note: ICTA runs a set of ecosystem initiatives alongside Spiralation, including incubation partnerships, mentoring networks, hackathons and market-access programmes. Cash support varies by initiative.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual initiatives open at different times; check icta.lk news for live calls.

eligibility.other_note: Sri Lankan technology startups and ecosystem enablers.

programmes.funder: Information and Communication Technology Agency of Sri Lanka (ICTA)
programmes.amount_note: Up to LKR 1.5 million as a grant covering infrastructure, training, business development, market access opportunities and mentoring.
programmes.deadline_note: The most recent published Spiralation cohort call closed on 26 May 2023. ICTA has not published a subsequent open call on the programme page.
programmes.reopen_note: Spiralation has run as periodic cohorts since 2013. ICTA's mandate has been reorganised under the Ministry of Digital Economy, which announced in 2026 that it would establish a government-seeded startup fund of funds. Watch icta.lk and mode.gov.lk for the next window.

procedure_steps.detail: Attend the applicant briefing session announced by ICTA when a cohort opens.
Submit the online application form before the published deadline.
Evaluation and pitching before the selection panel.
Grant and support disbursed to selected startups.

eligibility.other_note: Tech startups less than 3 years in existence, based in Sri Lanka.

programmes.source_snippet: If you are a tech startup less than 3 years in existence, you are eligible

programmes.name_local: Sri Lanka Startup Fund (government-seeded fund of funds)
programmes.name_en: Sri Lanka Startup Fund (government-seeded fund of funds)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Digital Economy, Government of Sri Lanka
programmes.amount_note: A fund of funds with initial seed capital from the government, announced for launch in January 2026 to address limited venture capital access. Corpus size and administering body were not published in the announcement.
programmes.deadline_note: Announced by Deputy Minister Eranga Weeraratne for launch in January 2026. Operating rules and an application route had not been published at the time of verification.
programmes.reopen_note: Watch mode.gov.lk for the fund's operating guidelines and the identity of the fund manager.

eligibility.other_note: Details not yet published. The stated intent is to support Sri Lankan startups to scale globally.

programmes.source_snippet: a fund of funds with initial seed capital from the government

programmes.name_local: EU-Sri Lanka Innovation Partnership (EUSLIP) / Start-ups Go Global
programmes.name_en: EU-Sri Lanka Innovation Partnership (EUSLIP) / Start-ups Go Global
programmes.funder: Sri Lanka Export Development Board with European Union support
programmes.amount_note: Soft-landing, internationalisation and market-access support for Sri Lankan startups going global, delivered through the startupsl.lk platform and an EU helpdesk. Cash grants are programme-specific.
programmes.deadline_note: Support is delivered through periodic cohorts and helpdesk services; check startupsl.lk for the live programme.

eligibility.other_note: Sri Lankan startups with export or international expansion ambitions.

programmes.name_en: Vidatha Programme (technology transfer to rural entrepreneurs)
programmes.funder: Ministry responsible for Science and Technology, Government of Sri Lanka
programmes.amount_note: Technology transfer, training and enterprise development support to rural and small entrepreneurs through Vidatha Resource Centres in divisional secretariats. Cash grants are limited and set locally.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made at the Vidatha Resource Centre in the applicant's divisional secretariat; there is no single national deadline. Confirm the programme's current ministerial home, which has changed with cabinet reorganisations.

eligibility.other_note: Rural entrepreneurs and small producers in Sri Lanka. Not a venture-style technology startup programme.
